concept:upc_ermessensueberpruefung.label: Leave to appeal and discretionary review (R. 220.2 to 220.4 RoP)
concept:upc_ermessensueberpruefung.definition: Case management orders and other orders not listed in R. 220.1 RoP can only be appealed with leave of the Court of First Instance (R. 220.2 RoP). If leave is refused, a request for discretionary review may be filed with the Court of Appeal within 15 days (R. 220.3 RoP); the standing judge decides on leave (R. 220.4 RoP).
concept:upc_ermessensueberpruefung.erlaeuterung: The Court of Appeal grants leave if the order is manifestly wrong or raises a question of principle. This route applies to decisions of the panel after review under R. 333 RoP, for example on access to the file (UPC CoA 2026), on setting the value of the dispute and on setting penalty payments (EOFlow/Insulet).

concept:upc_beschwer.label: Adverse effect and interest in appealing
concept:upc_beschwer.definition: An appeal or cross-appeal can only be lodged by a party adversely affected, in whole or in part, by the decision (R. 220.1 and R. 237 RoP). A cross-appeal that only seeks to change the reasoning of a decision favourable to the party is inadmissible (UPC CoA Abbott/Sinocare).
concept:upc_beschwer.erlaeuterung: The conditional counterclaimant is adversely affected if the Court of First Instance did not decide on the counterclaim because the condition was not fulfilled and the infringement claimant appeals (Emboline/AorticLab). Anyone who did not contest jurisdiction at first instance can no longer rely on it on appeal (Sinocare/Abbott).

concept:upc_wiederaufnahme.label: Rehearing (Art. 81 UPCA, R. 245 to 250 RoP)
concept:upc_wiederaufnahme.definition: After a final decision, the Court of Appeal may, on request, exceptionally grant a rehearing if a fact of a decisive nature is discovered which was unknown to the party requesting the rehearing – and only on the ground of an act qualified as a criminal offence by a final court decision of a national court –, or if there is a fundamental procedural defect (Art. 81(1) UPCA). Time limit: ten years from the decision, two months from discovery (Art. 81(2) UPCA).
concept:upc_wiederaufnahme.erlaeuterung: Rehearing is an extraordinary remedy; fundamental procedural defects under R. 247 RoP include, for example, a violation of the right to be heard or an incorrect composition of the panel (UPC CoA Suinno/Microsoft). Third parties acting in good faith are protected (Art. 81(4) UPCA).

concept:upc_up_rechtsrahmen.label: Legal framework of the Unitary Patent: UPReg, TranslReg, UPR, RFeesUPP, UP Guidelines
concept:upc_up_rechtsrahmen.definition: The Unitary Patent is based on two EU regulations adopted under enhanced cooperation (Art. 20 TEU): Regulation (EU) No 1257/2012 (UPReg) creates the European patent with unitary effect, Regulation (EU) No 1260/2012 (TranslReg) governs the translation arrangements. Both have been in force since 20 January 2013 and apply since 1 June 2023, the date of entry into force of the UPCA (Art. 18 UPReg, Art. 7 TranslReg). The procedure before the EPO is governed, as secondary law of the Select Committee of the Administrative Council (Art. 145 EPC), by the Rules relating to Unitary Patent Protection (UPR) and the Rules relating to Fees for Unitary Patent Protection (RFeesUPP).
concept:upc_up_rechtsrahmen.erlaeuterung: The regulations are Union law and thus the first source of law of the UPC (Art. 24(1)(a) UPCA). Substantive law is not contained in the UPReg: Art. 5(3) UPReg refers to the national law of the state determined under Art. 7 UPReg, which for all Contracting Member States is harmonised in Art. 25 to 30 UPCA. The EPO's practice is described in the UP Guidelines (April 2026 edition, in force since 1 April 2026, OJ EPO 2026, A6), issued by the President under R. 3 UPR; they are not legislation, but the EPO adheres to them until the UPC decides otherwise. 25 EU states take part in the enhanced cooperation (all except Spain and Croatia); only states that have ratified the UPCA can take part in the system (currently 18).

concept:upc_up_richtlinien.label: UP Guidelines of the EPO (Guidelines for Unitary Patent Protection)
concept:upc_up_richtlinien.definition: The Guidelines for Unitary Patent Protection describe the practice of the Unitary Patent Protection Division on the request for unitary effect, fees, compensation, re-establishment of rights, interruption, register entries and procedure. The President of the EPO issues them under R. 3 UPR in conjunction with Art. 10(2)(a) EPC; the April 2026 edition applies since 1 April 2026 (OJ EPO 2026, A6) and replaces the first edition of 1 April 2025.
concept:upc_up_richtlinien.erlaeuterung: Eight parts: 1 General (legal framework, UPC, territorial scope, Division), 2 Request for unitary effect, 3 Fees, 4 Compensation scheme, 5 Re-establishment of rights, 6 Interruption and stay, 7 Register (transfers, licences, licences of right), 8 Procedure before the Division (representation, time limits, legal remedies). The Guidelines are not legislation; the UPReg, TranslReg, UPR, RFeesUPP and UPCA are decisive, followed by their interpretation by the UPC. They are revised annually (each reflecting the position as at 1 December of the preceding year) and published only electronically; search, examination and opposition remain matters for the EPC Guidelines.

concept:upc_up_generationen.label: Territorial scope and generations of Unitary Patents
concept:upc_up_generationen.definition: A Unitary Patent has effect in the participating Member States in which the UPCA is in force on the date of registration of unitary effect (Art. 18(2) UPReg). The territorial scope remains unchanged for the entire term and is not extended to states that ratify the UPCA later; each further ratification creates a new “generation”.
concept:upc_up_generationen.erlaeuterung: On 1 June 2023 the system started with 17 states (Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, the Netherlands, Portugal, Slovenia, Sweden). Romania has been part of it since 1 September 2024: Unitary Patents registered from that date (second generation) have effect in 18 states, older ones still in 17. Before an announced accession, the proprietor may request a delay in registration in order to reach the new generation (OJ EPO 2024, A61); the one-month time limit of R. 6(1) UPR remains unaffected. The territorial scope of each Unitary Patent is shown in the register (R. 16(1)(g) UPR). However, the patent is eligible only if it was granted with the same claims for all 25 states of the enhanced cooperation, irrespective of where it then has effect.

concept:upc_antrag_einheitliche_wirkung.label: Request for unitary effect (R. 5 to 7 UPR)
concept:upc_antrag_einheitliche_wirkung.definition: The proprietor of the European patent files the request for unitary effect in writing in the language of the proceedings with the EPO, no later than one month after publication of the mention of grant in the European Patent Bulletin (R. 6(1) and 6(2) UPR; Art. 9(1)(g) UPReg). The request contains particulars of the proprietor and representative, the patent number and, during the transitional period, the translation under Art. 6 TranslReg. It is required that the patent was granted with the same claims for all participating Member States (R. 5(2)(a) UPR).
concept:upc_antrag_einheitliche_wirkung.erlaeuterung: The one-month time limit cannot be extended, but re-establishment of rights is available: within two months of expiry of the time limit, irrespective of when the cause of non-compliance was removed (R. 22(2) UPR). An early request is possible after the decision to grant (Form 2006A) but is processed only from the mention of grant. Where there are several proprietors, all must file the request; co-proprietors only for non-participating states cannot. If the request complies with R. 5(2) and R. 6 UPR, the Division registers unitary effect and communicates the date (R. 7(1) UPR, Form 7030); the patent has effect retroactively from the mention of grant (Art. 4(1) UPReg). Formal deficiencies under R. 6(2) UPR can be corrected within a non-extendable one-month time limit (R. 7(3) UPR), for which there is no re-establishment of rights (R. 22(6) UPR; Bodycap/EPO). If eligibility is lacking or the time limit has been missed, the request is rejected after the proprietor has been heard (R. 7(2) UPR), which can be challenged within three weeks under R. 97 RoP; national “safety nets” then sometimes still allow validation. The request is free of charge and can be withdrawn until the decision.

concept:upc_up_uebersetzung.label: Translation arrangements and transitional period (TranslReg)
concept:upc_up_uebersetzung.definition: After publication of the specification in the EPO language of the proceedings, no further translations are required for the Unitary Patent (Art. 3 TranslReg). During a transitional period of six years from 1 June 2023, extendable to a maximum of twelve years, a full translation of the specification must however be filed with the request for unitary effect: into English if the language of the proceedings was German or French, into another official EU language if it was English (Art. 6 TranslReg, R. 6(2)(d) UPR).
concept:upc_up_uebersetzung.erlaeuterung: The translation serves information purposes only and has no legal effect; the EPO does not examine it but publishes it (R. 18 UPR); correction under R. 139 EPC. In a dispute, the proprietor must, at the request of the alleged infringer, provide a full translation into an official language of the state of infringement or of domicile and, at the request of the court, into the language of its proceedings, in each case at its own expense (Art. 4(1) to 4(3) TranslReg). In damages claims, the court takes into account whether an SME, a natural person or a university acted in good faith before receiving the translation (Art. 4(4) TranslReg). In addition, the compensation scheme covers the translation costs of the application phase.

concept:upc_up_kompensation.label: Compensation scheme for translation costs (Art. 5 TranslReg, R. 8 to 11 UPR)
concept:upc_up_kompensation.definition: Anyone who filed the European patent application or Euro-PCT application in an official EU language other than German, English or French receives a lump sum of EUR 500 upon registration of the Unitary Patent (R. 11 UPR, Art. 4(1) RFeesUPP) if all proprietors and, where applicable, all original applicants are natural persons, SMEs, non-profit organisations, universities or public research organisations with their residence or principal place of business in an EU Member State (R. 8 UPR).
concept:upc_up_kompensation.erlaeuterung: The request must be filed together with the request for unitary effect (box in Form 7000) and contains a declaration of status (R. 9 UPR); the residence or place of business must be in the EU, not necessarily in a participating state. Compensation is granted only after registration of unitary effect and thereafter irrevocably, even if the status changes later (R. 10(1) and 10(2) UPR). In case of doubt the Division requests evidence, such as extracts from the commercial register; if the compensation was based on an incorrect declaration, it must be repaid together with an administrative fee of 50 % with the next renewal fee, failing which the patent lapses (R. 10(4) and R. 14 UPR, Art. 4(2) RFeesUPP). Compensation supplements the fee reduction under R. 7a EPC for applications filed in an admissible non-official language.

concept:upc_up_jahresgebuehren.label: Renewal fees for the Unitary Patent (Art. 11 and 12 UPReg; R. 13 and 14 UPR; Art. 2 RFeesUPP)
concept:upc_up_jahresgebuehren.definition: A single renewal fee in euro is payable to the EPO for the Unitary Patent, due for the years following the year in which the mention of grant was published, in each case on the last day of the month corresponding to the month of filing (Art. 11 UPReg, R. 13(1) and 13(2) UPR). The amounts are set out in item 1 of Art. 2(1) RFeesUPP (2nd year EUR 35 to 20th year EUR 4,855, “True Top 4”); anyone can pay, without mandatory representation.
concept:upc_up_jahresgebuehren.erlaeuterung: Payable at the earliest three months before the due date; six-month grace period with a 50 % additional fee (R. 13(3) UPR, item 2 of Art. 2(1) RFeesUPP), calculated “from month-end to month-end”. If the fee is not paid, the patent lapses retroactively as of the due date (R. 14(1)(b) and 14(2) UPR); the EPO notes the loss of rights (R. 112 EPC), and re-establishment of rights is possible within one year from the end of the grace period (R. 22 UPR). Special features: fees falling due within three months of notification of the registration communication can be paid within that period without an additional fee (R. 13(4) UPR); fees that would have fallen due between the mention of grant and the communication only become due with the communication (R. 13(5) UPR). With a statement on licences of right, the fee is reduced by 15 % (Art. 3 RFeesUPP). The EPO retains 50 % of the revenue, the rest goes to the participating states (Art. 13 UPReg). Classic bundle patents, by contrast, pay national renewal fees per state.

concept:upc_up_lizenzbereitschaft.label: Licences of right (Art. 8 UPReg, R. 12 UPR)
concept:upc_up_lizenzbereitschaft.definition: The proprietor of a Unitary Patent may file a statement with the EPO that he is prepared to allow any person to use the invention as a licensee in return for appropriate consideration (Art. 8(1) UPReg, R. 12(1) UPR). A licence obtained on this basis is treated as a contractual licence (Art. 8(2) UPReg); the renewal fees are reduced by 15 % from receipt of the statement (Art. 3 RFeesUPP).
concept:upc_up_lizenzbereitschaft.erlaeuterung: The statement (Form 7001) is registered free of charge; it is excluded as long as an exclusive licence is registered or a request for its registration is pending (R. 12(3) UPR), and afterwards no exclusive licence can be registered (R. 12(4) UPR). Withdrawal is possible at any time but only takes effect once the entire reduction has been repaid (R. 12(2) UPR). The UPC decides on the appropriate consideration (Art. 32(1)(h) UPCA). The model is the licence-of-right declaration under § 23 PatG. To be distinguished are licensing commitments to standardisation bodies (FRAND), which the EPO merely receives and notes in the register (Art. 9(1)(c) UPReg, R. 16(1)(k) UPR).

concept:upc_up_register.label: Register for unitary patent protection, transfers and licences
concept:upc_up_register.definition: The EPO keeps the Register for unitary patent protection as a separate part of the European Patent Register (Art. 9(1)(b) UPReg, R. 15 UPR). It contains the registration of unitary effect with date and territorial scope, transfers, licences, rights in rem, limitation, revocation, lapse, licences of right and licensing commitments (R. 16 UPR). A Unitary Patent can only be transferred in respect of all states together, but can be licensed for part of the territory (Art. 3(2) UPReg).
concept:upc_up_register.erlaeuterung: Entries are made on request under the EPC rules (R. 20(2)(b) UPR in conjunction with R. 22 to 24 EPC) against evidence, such as the transfer agreement; the administrative fee is waived for requests filed via MyEPO. A licence is recorded as exclusive if the proprietor and the licensee so request, and as a sub-licence if it is granted by a registered licensee. Which law applies to rights in rem and execution is determined by Art. 7 UPReg. Unitary Patents can be recognised in the register by the code “C0”; there is a separate part of the European Patent Bulletin for them (R. 17 UPR). Unlike with the bundle patent, the central registration replaces parallel registrations in the national registers.

concept:upc_up_vermoegen.label: Unitary Patent as an object of property (Art. 7 UPReg)
concept:upc_up_vermoegen.definition: As an object of property, the Unitary Patent is treated in its entirety and in all participating Member States as a national patent of the state in which, according to the European Patent Register, the applicant had his residence or principal place of business on the date of filing, or failing that a place of business (Art. 7(1) UPReg). Where there are several applicants, the first-named applicant who meets the requirement is decisive (Art. 7(2) UPReg). If none applies, German law applies as the law of the state where the EPO has its headquarters (Art. 7(3) UPReg).
concept:upc_up_vermoegen.erlaeuterung: This conflict-of-laws rule governs the transfer, pledging, execution and insolvency of the Unitary Patent. An applicant from a third state may voluntarily indicate a place of business on the filing date together with the request for unitary effect (R. 16(1)(w) UPR); if there is none, German law applies. The indication is not displayed if the UPCA is not in force in the state named at the date of registration. Infringement and its legal consequences, by contrast, are governed by Art. 5(3) UPReg, which leads to the UPCA.

concept:upc_up_abteilung.label: Unitary Patent Protection Division and proceedings before the EPO
concept:upc_up_abteilung.definition: The participating Member States have entrusted the EPO with the administration of the Unitary Patent under Art. 143 EPC (Art. 9 UPReg): requests for unitary effect, register, renewal fees, compensation, licences of right. The competent body is the Unitary Patent Protection Division, whose decisions are taken by a legally qualified member (R. 4 UPR). For the procedure, R. 20 UPR refers to the EPC: representation, right to be heard, notification, calculation of time limits, interruption, register entries.
concept:upc_up_abteilung.erlaeuterung: Particularities compared with EPC proceedings: time limits set by the Division are one to four months and cannot be extended (R. 20(4) UPR); no further processing (R. 135 EPC), but re-establishment of rights under R. 22 UPR; the request for unitary effect must be filed in the language of the proceedings, non-official languages are excluded; in request proceedings oral proceedings take place only at the proprietor's request and are not public (R. 21 UPR); a representative must be appointed specifically for the Unitary Patent, proprietors with their seat in an EPC state can act through employees, and anyone can pay renewal fees. The President may stay the registration procedure as a precaution (R. 3 UPR, sanctions cases 2024). Legal remedies lie not with the Boards of Appeal but with the UPC.

concept:upc_up_rechtsbehelf.label: Action against decisions of the EPO on the Unitary Patent (Art. 32(1)(i) and Art. 66 UPCA; R. 85 to 98 RoP)
concept:upc_up_rechtsbehelf.definition: Decisions of the Unitary Patent Protection Division are challenged not by an appeal to the Boards of Appeal but by an action before the UPC (Art. 9(3) UPReg; R. 23 UPR; Art. 32(1)(i) UPCA). The Court may annul or alter the decision (Art. 66 UPCA). The action must be lodged with the Registry within two months of service (R. 88 RoP); against the rejection of the request for unitary effect, the expedited procedure under R. 97 RoP applies, with a time limit of three weeks and a decision by the standing judge within three weeks (R. 97.4 RoP).
concept:upc_up_rechtsbehelf.erlaeuterung: The central division is competent (Art. 33(9) UPCA; Annex II UPCA), the language of the proceedings is the language of the patent; mandatory representation does not apply here (Art. 48(7) UPCA). Interlocutory revision by the EPO (R. 24 UPR, R. 91 RoP: two months after service of the admissible action) is excluded in the procedure under R. 97 RoP, because R. 85.2 RoP excludes expedited procedures and R. 97 RoP is lex specialis (UPC CoA Bodycap/EPO). The EPO is bound by the decision of the UPC (R. 1(1) UPR). The rejection of compensation, of re-establishment of rights and the decision on a loss of rights under R. 112(2) EPC can also be challenged.

concept:upc_durchsetzungsrl_bezug.label: UPCA and Enforcement Directive 2004/48/EC
concept:upc_durchsetzungsrl_bezug.definition: Art. 56 to 69 and Art. 80 UPCA implement the measures, procedures and remedies of the Enforcement Directive for the UPC: order to produce evidence (Art. 59 UPCA, Art. 6 IPRED), preservation of evidence (Art. 60 UPCA, Art. 7 IPRED), information (Art. 67 UPCA, Art. 8 IPRED), provisional measures (Art. 62 UPCA, Art. 9 IPRED), corrective measures (Art. 64 UPCA, Art. 10 IPRED), injunction (Art. 63 UPCA, Art. 11 IPRED), damages (Art. 68 UPCA, Art. 13 IPRED), costs (Art. 69 UPCA, Art. 14 IPRED), publication (Art. 80 UPCA, Art. 15 IPRED). As Union law, the Directive is a source of law with priority (Art. 24(1)(a) UPCA).
concept:upc_durchsetzungsrl_bezug.erlaeuterung: The Court of Appeal interprets the UPCA provisions in conformity with the Directive, for example the standard of a sufficient degree of certainty in light of Art. 9(3) IPRED (NanoString/10x). For the exam, the parallel to German law is valuable: the same Directive lies behind §§ 139 to 140e PatG and §§ 14, 18, 19 to 19c MarkenG. Anyone who knows trade mark law already knows the structure of the UPC's remedies.
